claims.text: As-cast HfNbTaTiZr has high intrinsic lattice distortion caused by chemical and atomic-size mismatches.
Annealing between 600°C and 1000°C can increase atomic ordering in HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed annealing treatment can avoid significant secondary-phase formation.
Annealing-induced atomic ordering reduces atomic-scale lattice distortion in HfNbTaTiZr.
Annealing-induced atomic ordering reduces local chemical inhomogeneities in HfNbTaTiZr.
Lattice strain fields impede dislocation motion in HfNbTaTiZr.
Increased atomic ordering lowers the density of dislocation-impeding lattice strain fields.
Reducing lattice strain fields through annealing increases dislocation mobility and lowers elevated-temperature yield strength.
Annealed HfNbTaTiZr will have lower yield strength than as-cast HfNbTaTiZr at 0.5–0.8 Tm.
Annealed HfNbTaTiZr will have a softer elastic modulus than the as-cast alloy at 0.5–0.8 Tm.
Annealing will produce a measurable but modest change in the thermal expansion coefficient of HfNbTaTiZr.
The annealing-induced property changes will be most pronounced between approximately 0.5 and 0.8 Tm.
As-cast HfNbTaTiZr typically has higher yield strength than its annealed counterpart because of lattice distortion.
As-cast HfNbTaTiZr typically has a stiffer elastic response than its annealed counterpart because of lattice distortion.
Temperature-dependent changes in dislocation mobility or controlling slip mode could concurrently affect the measured strength response.
The hypothesis is intended to apply only from approximately 0.5 to 0.8 Tm and when significant secondary phases do not develop.
